citation.authors: van Galen KA, Booij J, Schrantee A, Adriaanse SM, Unmehopa UA, Fliers E, Schwartz GJ, DiLeone RJ, et al.
citation.title: The response to prolonged fasting in hypothalamic serotonin transporter availability is blunted in obesity

population.description: Nineteen men aged 50-75 y (enrolment criterion) who completed a randomised crossover of 12 h vs 24 h fasting: 10 lean (BMI <25) and 9 with obesity (BMI >30); no medication except thyroid hormone, antihypertensive and lipid-lowering drugs, no somatic disorder except treated hypothyroidism, hypertension, dyslipidaemia. No glucose tolerance test reported, so each group is unselected. Age and BMI are given per group (Table 1) as arm overrides.

protocols.name: lean_fast12
protocols.description: Venous blood sample of the lean men after a 12-h overnight fast (stated: 'a 12-h overnight fast'; fast = no food or drink except tap water, started exactly 12 h before the first brain scan, after a 72-h eucaloric diet 50/30/20 % carbohydrate/fat/protein). The sample time and duration are not printed. The paper's own clock puts the end of the 12-h fast at the first brain scan, 10-12 AM (the 24-h fast 'started at 10-12 AM on the day before neuroimaging'), so minute 0 is set to 10.5 h and a 30 min run-in is assumed.

protocols.name: obese_fast12
protocols.description: Venous blood sample of the men with obesity after a 12-h overnight fast (stated: 'a 12-h overnight fast'; fast = no food or drink except tap water, started exactly 12 h before the first brain scan, after a 72-h eucaloric diet 50/30/20 % carbohydrate/fat/protein). The sample time and duration are not printed. The paper's own clock puts the end of the 12-h fast at the first brain scan, 10-12 AM (the 24-h fast 'started at 10-12 AM on the day before neuroimaging'), so minute 0 is set to 10.5 h and a 30 min run-in is assumed.
